purpose: Prove the existing local Rea MCP service and Ghidra backend with an actual bounded static query, then capture pseudocode, assembly and direct callees for only 0x180284200, the observed pointer-cache growth helper. One temporary import, no target execution or automatic expansion.
execution_requirements: Before dispatch, verify the target SHA256 and actual MCP tools/list schemas against this plan; stop on mismatch.
The calls array already contains normal-path open, close, and session checks; do not add duplicate lifecycle calls.
Use only the fixed Engine target and provider. Do not launch or load the target DLL for execution, change target bytes, query saves, or expand the tool allowlist.
Dispatch sequentially, save each raw result under its unique label, and retain provider evidence and limitations.
Stop the remaining plan on errors, denial, unavailable provider, unexpected target identity, or unavailable analysis; do not silently substitute another backend or guess callees.
If stopped while a target is open, perform only necessary close_binary cleanup when permitted, within the total call budget, and record whether closure is confirmed.
The final session result must confirm no active target; verify the original Engine SHA256 again after closure.
Calls to newly discovered direct callees are not included in this batch. Review returned addresses and scope before preparing another bounded batch.

Use one Rea/Ghidra process tree and a 512M Java heap. Require at least 6 GiB free physical memory before launch; sample every 2 seconds and stop the owned process tree below 5 GiB to leave a margin above the requested 4 GiB system reserve. This is sampled monitoring, not an OS memory reservation.
